source_checks.finding: Page supports the storage rule ("If your Microsoft cloud storage is full, you cannot send or receive email."), the 25 MB attachment limit, and the signature rule (remove the signature and re-send). Page also supports the account check: update the password if changed recently, and the temporary block for unusual sign-in activity with a link using the text "unblock your Outlook.com account". The page does not show the linked article's title, so the title quoted in the target is unsupported.

Page supports the excerpt verbatim: "If you can't sign in to your account, use the Microsoft account sign-in helper." Page also supports the account check step (password update, temporary block for unusual sign-in activity). Applicability to Outlook.com accounts confirmed.

Apple page is for iPhone and iPad Mail fetch settings (Settings, Apps, Mail, Mail Accounts, Fetch New Data; Automatically is the default on iOS 11 and later and iPadOS). The user uses Outlook.com in a web browser, not the iPhone Mail app, so this distractor does not apply to this user and is correctly unused.

required_actions.action: Check Microsoft cloud storage and mailbox storage, since a full storage stops sending and receiving
If storage is not full, check the account
Update the password if it was changed recently
If the account may be temporarily blocked for unusual sign-in activity, unblock it through the linked article (link text: unblock your Outlook.com account)
If sign-in fails, use the Microsoft account sign-in helper
Attachments over 25 MB cannot be sent
If a signature causes an error, remove it and resend

findings: Step 4 quotes an article title, "Learn how to unblock your Outlook.com account", and calls it a Microsoft Support article. The Outlook.com page only shows the link text "unblock your Outlook.com account" and does not give any article title. The title is invented.
correction_required: In step 4, replace the quoted title with the page's own wording, for example: "4. If your account may be temporarily blocked because of unusual sign-in activity, follow the link to the Microsoft Support article about how to unblock your Outlook.com account." Do not quote a title that is not on the page.
